answer: Each identity must serve one unique shard of public data: the network assigns a random shard, then spot-checks demand its bytes on short notice. One operator running a thousand clones cannot serve them from a single disk, because duplicate shards are detected and struck off, so farm cost grows with each clone's storage and bandwidth, not with a script minting keys. A harbor berths one ship per slip, and that anchor of real provision becomes the gate. Limits: a rich attacker can still buy disks, and spot-checks fail if challengers collude; a plume of identical instant replies exposes the farm.
